Septic Inspections: Larimer vs. Weld County

When buying a home or land with a septic system in Northern Colorado, knowing the county-specific rules can save you time, money, and surprises during escrow. Here’s a breakdown of how Larimer and Weld County differ when it comes to septic inspections.

Larimer County: Septic Transfer of Title is Required

In Larimer County, septic systems must go through a Transfer of Title process during any real estate transaction. This includes:

  • A cleanout must be installed and accessible
  • The system must be inspected by a county-approved provider
  • Documentation must be submitted and approved before closing
Tip: Sellers in Larimer should start the process early to avoid delays. Buyers should request all paperwork during the offer period.

More info: Larimer County Septic Program

Weld County: Buyer-Initiated Inspections

Weld County does not require a septic inspection by default. However, buyers should take the initiative:

  • Hire a certified inspector to evaluate the tank and leach field
  • Ask for records of pumping and maintenance
  • Budget for potential repairs or replacement
Tip: Just because it’s not required doesn’t mean it’s not essential. A failed system can cost $10,000–$30,000+ to replace.

More info: Weld County Septic Program

Which County is Stricter?

Larimer has stricter compliance rules with clear timelines. Weld provides more buyer flexibility but less oversight. Knowing the difference helps you stay in control during negotiations and inspections.
